user.text:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

history.assistant:
Built Bookkeep, a small account-free reading tracker. It shows currently reading and finished books, lets you add a title, author, and notes, mark a book finished, and open a shareable page for each book. Books persist in data/books.json across restarts.

Run npm start, then open http://localhost:3000. A book link is only shareable with someone who can reach the server; localhost links work only on your machine.

Verification passed: npm test (2 tests) and npm run build (syntax check), both exit code 0.

tool_steps.assistant: I’ll inspect the existing app structure, then add the book list, form, detail links, and JSON-file storage using the project’s conventions.
The repository has no app framework or existing UI. I’ll use a small Node server with server-rendered pages and a JSON file, so it won’t need a database or frontend build step.

# Bookkeep

A small, account-free reading tracker. Add books with a title, author, and optional notes; view your currently reading and finished shelves; open a book's own URL; and mark books finished.

## Run

Requires Node.js 20 or newer.

```sh
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000. For automatic server restarts while editing, use `npm run dev`.

Books are saved to `data/books.json` by default. That folder is ignored by git so personal reading data is not accidentally committed. Set `BOOKS_FILE` to an absolute file path to store the data elsewhere, or `PORT` to use another port.

A book's `/books/<id>` URL can be shared with someone who can reach your running server. A localhost link is only reachable on your own machine; sharing over a network requires hosting the app somewhere reachable and keeping the JSON file on persistent storage. There are no accounts or access controls, so anyone who can reach the server can view and change the library.

Run `npm test` for integration tests and `npm run build` for a syntax check.
